source: experiments/flow_events.py mandeb: IMF PortWatch daily tanker capacity through Bab el-Mandeb, the Strait of Hormuz and the Cape of Good Hope (AIS-derived, fetched 2026-10-24) to 2026-10-18, as a share of each chokepoint's 2019-2024 mean; PortWatch daily tanker exports at Yanbu (port570) and seven Gulf ports (fetched 2026-10-24). The events and the bypass are those of notes/flow-events.md. Nothing here is synthetic.
per_src: one point of Bab el-Mandeb's normal tanker tonnage in points of Hormuz's: the 2019-2024 means, 0.885 and 2.400 million deadweight tonnes a day

diversion_2024.label: 2024 Houthi diversion
diversion_2024.news: 2023-11-19: Houthis seize the Galaxy Leader; 2023-12-18: BP and the big container lines pause Red Sea transits; 2024-01-12: US and UK strikes on the Houthis
diversion_2024.rule: lost: the pre-level (days -29..-7) minus the mean share from day 0 to +120 trading days; rerouted: the Cape of Good Hope's gain over the same window, in Bab el-Mandeb tonnage

blockade_2026.label: Sep 2026 Houthi blockade of Saudi shipping
blockade_2026.what: Houthis declare a blockade of Saudi shipping
blockade_2026.rule: lost: the pre-level before 2026-07-20 (days -29..-7) minus the mean share over 2026-09; cape_gain: the Cape's gain over the same, in Bab el-Mandeb tonnage; yanbu_lost: the share of Yanbu's extra exports since the closure began that was gone in 2026-09

yanbu_bypass.rule: Yanbu's tanker exports above their pre-closure level, as a share of the seven Gulf ports' lost exports, over every observed day of the closure (the bypass the flow-premium curve, fitted to those days, has built in); share_before_blockade stops the day before the declared blockade

combined: Hormuz-equivalent loss = Hormuz points lost + Bab el-Mandeb points lost × hormuz_per_mandeb_point × (1 − the 2024 diversion's rerouted share) + Hormuz points lost × yanbu_bypass.share × the share of the Yanbu bypass lost (by default the share of Bab el-Mandeb's flow lost). Brent's premium is per point lost, so it takes the whole sum; the chain's scenario tables stop at 100, so their numbers are read there (eq) and understate a larger loss. Assumptions: any Red Sea loss reroutes round the Cape as in 2024; Yanbu's extra exports all sail south through Bab el-Mandeb and are not rerouted; the bypass's barrels count one for one as Hormuz points, as the Net Hormuz points column of notes/flow-events.md does.
